document.title: Collision Resistance of Single-Layer Neural Nets

candidate.title: Collision Resistance of the Symmetric Binary Perceptron
candidate.subtitle: An intermediate window of kappa where neither the algorithms nor the hardness arguments reach
candidate.one_line: For some alpha < 1 there is an intermediate window of kappa in which the symmetric binary perceptron is collision resistant against polynomial-time algorithms.
candidate.status_note: Posed as a displayed Open Question and called a central open challenge. The source gives an efficient online collision finder for small kappa and an overlap-gap-based online lower bound for a different, randomized activation -- introduced precisely because the SBP's own collision space resists a first-moment analysis.
candidate.progress_note: For small kappa the SBP falls inside the positive-tail algorithmic window; for very large kappa collisions become trivial. The middle is reached by neither technique, and the source names kappa ~ 0.675, alpha ~ 0.9 as a concrete point inside it.

parameters.meaning: collision ratio; the open regime is alpha < 1
the SBP threshold; the open window is 1/log n << kappa << 1/sqrt(alpha)
extensiveness of the collision: x^T y <= (1-delta) n

candidate.why_interesting: It is the precise gap between an algorithm and a hardness argument that the same paper supplies, on a canonical object, with a concrete parameter point named inside the gap.
candidate.why_clean: One model, one parameter window, one algorithm class.

quotes.quote: For some α < 1, does there exist an intermediate window of κ
Resolving whether SBP is collision resistant in this middle regime, for some α < 1 and some κ, remains a central open challenge.
The difficult case is the intermediate window, where the positive-tail escape route no longer applies but no OGP-based hardness result is known for collision finding.
This extra randomness removes the rigid alignments that make the SBP collision space difficult to analyze, while preserving the obstruction to the positive-tail algorithm.
We leave confirming this conjecture, or finding algorithmic counterexamples, as an open direction for future work.
Neither known algorithmic techniques nor hardness arguments currently apply when κ lies in an intermediate window

check.notes: The Open Question is verbatim on page 5 and is recorded in the affirmative purely because a statement needs a direction; a remark says so explicitly and notes the source predicts nothing. Two page claims were corrected by grounding: the 'central open challenge' and 'difficult case' passages are on page 3, not 4, and the 'neither known algorithmic techniques' passage is on page 5, not 4. The paper's numbered Conjecture 1.4 is a different statement -- it concerns the randomized oscillating activation, not the SBP -- and is recorded as a neighbour rather than merged in.
